citation: Fan, Xiaolei, and Kin Wing Kevin Chan. 2022. 香港粵語「咗」的語法特點：與北京話「了1」的比較 [Grammatical properties of zo 咗 in Hong Kong Cantonese: A comparative study with le1 了1 in Beijing Mandarin]. Language and Linguistics 23(3):371–410.
locator: Abstract; article pp. 371–410; discussion of complex VP placement, realis/irrealis distribution, completion, boundedness, and clause completeness
verified_claim: Analyzes verbal zo2 as perfective; reports that in complex verbal material it attaches to the first verb under the profiles studied; argues that Cantonese strong VO order permits substantial postverbal material and disfavors sentence-final placement relative to Mandarin le1; distinguishes V+laa and V+zo+laa.
limitation: The paper discusses several completion, boundedness, temporal, and current-relevance analyses and uses a small internal consultant set for some judgements. Its first-verb generalization must not be transferred mechanically to resultative and inner-aspect clusters that other sources analyze as V-IAP-zo2.

citation: Sio, Joanna Ut-Seong, and Francis Bond. 2025. Inner and outer aspect in Cantonese. HPSG 2025 conference paper / Proceedings of the 32nd International Conference on Head-Driven Phrase Structure Grammar.
locator: pp. 180–195; data section; examples 2a–c; Tables 1–2; outer-aspect analysis
profile: Outer perfective zo2 and postverbal particle ordering
verified_claim: Classifies zo2 as an outer perfective marker; gives exact V-zo2-object `我食咗麵`; distinguishes simple V-OAP from V-IAPi-OAP and V-IAPe-OAP; states the postverbal order V-IAP-OAP and gives `食飽(咗)麵` and `食完(咗)麵` as distinct valid profiles.
limitation: The HPSG analysis is preliminary and illustrative rather than exhaustive. It does not establish unrestricted predicate-object combinations or require Canto Span to adopt its exact formal representation.

citation: Yip, Ka-Fai. 2025. Inner Aspect in Cantonese. FLaP FIRST 1:15–36.
locator: pp. 15–24; verbal template (1); definition (2); examples 4–7; completion discussion footnote 2
profile: Outer zo2, resultative complements, and inner aspect
verified_claim: Places resultative verbal complements closest to the root, then inner aspect, then outer perfective zo2; establishes that RVC and inner-aspect material can precede zo2; gives `我寫咗一封信，但未寫完` to show that Chinese perfective indicates an endpoint without guaranteeing completion of the whole event.
limitation: The paper focuses on inner aspect rather than the complete object system. Its endpoint analysis does not deny frequent completion or current-relevance inferences in context.

citation: Matthews, Stephen, and Virginia Yip. Cantonese: A Comprehensive Grammar, multimedia Chapter 11, Aspect and verbal particles.
locator: Sections 11.1–11.3; exact perfective and postverbal-particle examples
profile: Cantonese perfective and postverbal particle profiles
verified_claim: Treats zo2 as perfective, gives ordinary postverbal placement, and separately presents resultative, directional, quantifying, adversative, experiential, progressive, continuous, delimitative, inchoative, and habitual particles.
limitation: Edited grammar examples establish ordinary profiles and contrasts but do not define every lexical compatibility, object type, or parser constituency.

citation: Yip, Virginia, and Stephen Matthews. 2000. Basic Cantonese: A Grammar and Workbook. Routledge.
locator: Unit 18 printed pp. 93–96 / PDF pp. 105–108; Unit 23 printed pp. 122–123 / PDF pp. 134–135
verified_claim: Provides multiple overt V-zo2-object examples, analyzes zo2 as perfective, and states that verb morphology does not locate an event in past time by itself; illustrates final `未` questions separately.
limitation: The pedagogical source often describes events as complete and discusses result/current relevance. It does not settle all semantic theories or justify arbitrary action-verb and object combinations.

citation: Wong, Anita Mei-Yin, Candice Chi-Hang Cheung, Joanna Man-Wai Lo, and Elaine Kit-Hung Wan. 2022. Grammatical Analysis of Cantonese Samples. In Understanding Development and Disorder in Cantonese Using Language Sample Analysis. Routledge.
locator: Aspect-marker section; examples including 搬緊屋, 幫我揸住個杯, 睇吓我, and perfective zo2 definition
verified_claim: Classifies zo2 as perfective and distinguishes it from progressive gan2, locative progressive hai2dou6, continuous zyu6, experiential gwo3, habitual hoi1/gwaan3, delimitative haa5, and inchoative markers.
limitation: The clinical language-sample framework glosses zo2 as indicating a completed event; it is a practical annotation description, not evidence that completion is logically entailed in every context.

citation: Wong, Anita M.-Y., Stephanie F. Stokes, and Paul Fletcher. 2009. Aspectual asymmetries in the mental representation of events: Role of lexical and grammatical aspect. Memory & Cognition 37:587–595.
locator: Materials and methods; paired gan2/zo2 stimuli such as `媽媽焗咗個蛋糕`
profile: Experimental V-zo2-object use across lexical aspect
verified_claim: Uses audio-recorded, matched Cantonese sentences with postverbal gan2 and zo2 before overt nominal material; includes activity and accomplishment predicates and tests 83 Hong Kong Cantonese-speaking secondary students.
limitation: Experimental stimuli demonstrate conventional structure and processing effects, not open-class productivity, full grammaticality boundaries, or the semantics of every token.

citation: Wong, Anita M.-Y., Stephanie F. Stokes, and Paul Fletcher. 2003. Collocational diversity in perfective aspect zo2 use in Cantonese children with SLI. Journal of Multilingual Communication Disorders 1(2):132–140.
locator: Conversational-sample method and zo2 predicate-type analysis
verified_claim: Analyzes 900-utterance conversational samples and measures the number and proportion of predicate types occurring with zo2, providing independent usage evidence that zo2 combines with multiple predicates in child Cantonese.
limitation: Child-language collocational diversity cannot establish adult unrestricted productivity or the complete object-bearing construction boundary.

citation: Wong, Anita M.-Y., Paul Fletcher, and Stephanie F. Stokes. 2004. The expression of aspect in Cantonese-speaking children with specific language impairment. Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research 47:733–750.
locator: Perfective zo2 elicitation task; change-of-state and verb/compound examples
profile: Zo2 after verbs and compound predicates
verified_claim: States that zo2 follows simple verbs and resultative compounds in elicited change-of-state descriptions; examples include simple transitive verb plus object and compounds such as pour-spill, blow-extinguish, sleep-asleep, hit-open, cut-open, and iron-straight.
limitation: Elicitation targets were designed to prompt aspect marking and often emphasize completion. They demonstrate order and lexical diversity but do not settle spontaneous frequency or every adult semantic interpretation.
